description: Well-documented, real per-company data points found during research that are not covered by the 27 official survey questions but could plausibly matter to a values-driven investor. Logged here for review -- NOT added to the official question set. Each entry: a proposed survey question in the same plain-language 1-5-importance style, the supporting data source, and current coverage.

candidates.proposed_question: Prioritizing companies with a validated Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) emissions-reduction commitment
candidates.rationale: SBTi validation is a much stronger, independently-verified signal of real decarbonization commitment than the 10-K keyword scan used for Q1/Q2, which only detects whether a company *mentions* climate/renewable topics in its business description, not whether it has a validated target.

candidates.rationale: A common values-investing screen (comparable in spirit to founder_led/family_owned in Q24) that the official 27-question list does not cover. Implemented and populated for all 503 companies as the `women_led` field -- see schema/company_schema.json's `additional_criteria` section for the field's data dictionary entry.
candidates.source: DEF 14A proxy statement (EDGAR) -- see find_ceo_gender_signal() in scripts/lib.py
candidates.coverage_status: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20 via scripts/fix_women_led.py, run across all 503 companies (503/503 populated: 40 True, 334 False, 129 None). Identifies the CEO's surname via a name+title-adjacency regex, then reads the filing's own honorific (Mr./Ms./Mrs.) or, failing that, a majority of pronoun references (she/her vs he/his) for that specific named person -- never guessed from a first name. Required three full backfill passes to reach a clean result -- each of the first two surfaced a real, distinct false-positive class only found by spot-checking against public knowledge, not by the initial ~30-ticker regression test: (1) some companies (P&G) use "Chief Executive Officer" as an internal title for multiple business-segment heads, not just the overall corporate CEO, so raw mention-frequency alone picked the wrong person -- fixed by preferring a name whose matched title includes Chair(man/woman) language, since segment heads are essentially never also Board Chair; (2) that same chair-tag fix then over-fired on a SINGLE stray mention of an outside director's title *at their own separate company* (Disney's board-bio table describes director Mary Barra using her actual GM title, which briefly outranked Disney's real CEO Robert Iger) -- fixed by requiring a chair-tagged candidate to independently clear the same >=2-mentions bar the raw-frequency path already requires. The third full run was cross-checked in full: every one of the 40 True hits verified against public knowledge, and zero were resolved via the chair-tag override path (i.e. the specific code path both prior bugs lived in never fired in the final, clean run).
candidates.confidence_if_implemented: Low (flattened-text regex heuristic reading the filing's own gendered language -- same class of caveat as founder_led/family_owned, not a verified/audited fact)
